title: classify-and-resolve log record
description: One JSON object per line (JSONL). A record is a Classification or a Resolution from references/model.md, wrapped in an envelope that names the log id, time and pipeline version. Field names are a stable contract; the scripts enforce them without a JSON Schema library.

log_id.description: Unique across the log. Becomes a Case's added_because.

at.description: ISO 8601 date or date-time the record was written.

item.description: Classification only, optional: the Item, logged once (usually on cascade step 0) so the log can become evaluation cases.

label.description: A concept id from the pipeline's scheme, or the reserved value unclassified.

level.description: exact for the class the step chose; broader when fallback: broader labeled a low-confidence item with the chosen class's broader concept.

rationale.description: Optional. Why the classifier chose or abstained; decision models give none. #tag tokens are rationale tags that unclassified_report.py groups by.

evidence.description: What the decision rests on, typed: a fired rule, an observed fact, a question-set answer.

model_version.description: Model steps: the pinned model version the question set's adapter reported.

output.description: The resolver's output, of its declared output_type; null when none.

corrected_label.description: The misroute signal: the class the item should have had.

kind.description: rule: a rule fired; observed: a fact from real data, such as usage in shipped code or a past decision; answer: a decision-questions answer.

ref.description: The rule id, the data source, or the question id.

value.description: What it said: the matched text, the observed value, the answer given.

source.description: Where the item came from: a queue, an inbox, a folder.

payload.description: The item as the classifier saw it; becomes the Case input.
